niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: Your Phone Motion Sensor Is Reading Your Passwords
ideas.angle: Demonstrates how mobile websites read motion sensors without permission to decode keypresses via vibration physics, prompting viewers to check their browser permission settings immediately.

hook.en: Your phone knows what you type before you hit send.

ideas.reason: Recent cybersecurity alerts highlight that mobile gyroscopes and accelerometers can infer PINs and keystrokes with over 80% accuracy without triggering OS permission popups, driving massive paranoia and immediate verification comments.
sources: Newcastle University Study on Gyroscope Keylogging
Wired: How Motion Sensors Can Spy on Keystrokes
ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

ideas.title: The 1-Second Clipboard Trap Exposing Snooping Apps
ideas.angle: Guides the viewer through a real-time live test copying a burner phrase to expose which background apps silently read their clipboard every time they launch.

hook.en: Copy this exact word right now.

ideas.reason: Clipboard hijacking and background paste access remain top-tier viral privacy concerns; viewers love interactive commands where their screen gives immediate visual feedback (e.g., paste notifications).
sources: Krebs on Security: Mobile Clipboard Snooping Exploits

ideas.title: The 5-Second Blink Glitch Exposing AI Deepfakes
ideas.angle: Shows a lightning-fast visual trick to spot real-time AI face-swappers during video calls by forcing them to turn sideways or counting abnormal blink intervals.

hook.en: Look closely at their eyes right now.

ideas.reason: Surging real-time deepfake video scams on FaceTime and WhatsApp have made biometric verification tips go hyper-viral across social media platforms.
sources: MIT Media Lab: Detecting Deepfakes Using Biological Signals
University at Buffalo: Deepfake Blink Inconsistency Research
FBI Cyber Division PSA on Synthetic Media and Live Video Manipulation
